title: Tiered routing economics and fallback policy — spot vs on-demand (working draft)
content:
Purpose
This working draft explores a tiered smart-routing cost model that combines fallback tiers, region-aware routing, and a spot vs on-demand provisioning strategy. The goal is practical guidance for routing policy defaults and a small spreadsheet we can use to estimate end-to-end cost deltas for customer workloads.

Scope and audience
- Audience: product-optimize, serving-runtime, infra-cost, solutions-eng
- Scope: per-request routing decisions (model variant selection + region/capacity tiering), fallback behavior under capacity pressure, spot preemption assumptions, and monthly cost implications. Not covering: detailed infra-level billing reconciliation, reserved capacity contracts (separate doc).

High-level idea
We model routing as a hierarchy of choices for each request:
- Primary: local region (lowest latency) using on-demand or reserved capacity if available
- Secondary (fallback tier 1): cross-region low-cost spot pools (if latency budget allows)
- Tertiary (fallback tier 2): hosted on-demand in another region or lower-capacity model variant (cheaper quantized model)
- Last resort: degrade to cached response or queue (with SLO violation).

This doc attempts a lightweight cost spreadsheet and recommendations for default policy thresholds (latency budget, spot max-preempt, fallback window).

Assumptions (baseline workload)
- Traffic: 10M tokens/day, 300k requests/day, avg 33 tokens per request.
- Model variants: full-precision (base), 4-bit quantized (q4), and small-encoder variant for short contexts.
- Performance: base model throughput 120 tokens/sec on a GPU; q4 throughput 180 tokens/sec; small-encoder 300 tokens/sec.
- Pricing (illustrative): on-demand GPU cost = $9.00/hr; spot GPU cost = $2.70/hr (30% preemptible availability assumed); cross-region egress = $0.02/1000 tokens equivalent (simplified).
- KV cache hit reduces token generation by 40% on average; we assume cache hit rate 25% for this workload.

Mini spreadsheet (monthlyized, simplified)
Columns: Scenario | Monthly GPU-hours | GPU cost | Egress est | Total est | Notes
Rows: baseline-on-demand, tiered-spot-first, aggressive-quantize-fallback

Scenario table (numbers rounded)
- baseline-on-demand: 2200 GPU-hrs / mo | $19,800 | $60 | $19,860 | single-region, no spot
- tiered-spot-first: 1800 GPU-hrs spot + 400 GPU-hrs on-demand | $5,000 + $3,600 = $8,600 | $75 | $8,675 | prefers spot in other regions up to preempt limit, falls to on-demand for bursts
- aggressive-quantize-fallback: 1600 GPU-hrs spot + 800 GPU-hrs on-demand | $4,320 + $7,200 = $11,520 | $65 | $11,585 | uses q4 variant for 40% requests when lat budget allows

Estimated monthly deltas vs baseline
- tiered-spot-first vs baseline: ~56% lower cost
- aggressive-quantize-fallback vs baseline: ~42% lower cost

Important caveats
- Spot availability: we conservatively assume 70% availability (30% preemption) which drives need for on-demand fallback capacity. If availability is lower (e.g., 50%), on-demand fallback costs rise non-linearly.
- Latency budget: cross-region fallback adds RTT; for 50–100ms latency budgets this is acceptable, for <40ms it is not. We need route-level latency budgets in the API to enable safe fallbacks.
- Egress and inter-region network costs can offset spot savings for very chatty workloads — we include a simplified egress estimate but actual billing will vary by cloud/region.

Policy knobs proposed (defaults + rationale)
1) spot-first fraction (per-route): default 60% of capacity routed to spot pools when estimated latency budget > 80ms; rationale: capture majority of spot savings while keeping fallback headroom.
2) max-preempt-window: 90s warm drain and automatic reroute; rationale: avoids immediate user-facing failures, buys time to shift to on-demand.
3) model-variant fallback order: prefer quantized variant before cross-region on-demand when output quality degradation is tolerable; rationale: avoids egress and can cheaply increase capacity.
4) cross-region allowed list: per-customer/regulatory constraint; default: only regions in same geo (NA <-> NA, EU <-> EU).
5) cache-first threshold: if KV cache hit rate > 30% for a route, increase spot-first fraction to 80% (saves tokens and reduces compute need).

Scenario simulation notes (how to run)
- Input: per-route latency SLO, token distribution, cache hit rate, expected burst percentiles.
- Steps: 1) simulate steady-state throughput on spot pools with preemption events (Poisson) 2) model failover to on-demand + model-variant shifts 3) compute monthly GPU-hours required and cost 4) add egress, storage, and minor infra overheads (10%).
- Quick prototype: I built a small single-sheet simulation (local csv) that uses the above assumptions; moving to a proper google sheet with scenario toggles is next.

Open questions / TODOs
- We need empirical spot preemption stats per region and instance type (ask infra for historical 12-month churn).
- How do we represent quantized-quality impact in SLOs? Product to own a quality metric mapping (accuracy delta -> allowed usage share).
- Should we expose a simple "cost-savvy" routing preset in Console (e.g., Balanced / Cost-Optimized / Low-Latency)? If so, map defaults to our knobs above.
- Validate cross-region egress pricing for enterprise customers on committed contracts (could be cheaper).
- Check legal/regulatory constraints for cross-region routing for customers in EU/UK.

Recommendations (short-term)
- Build a canonical google sheet with scenario toggles: spot availability, latency SLO, cache hit, token mix, model variant split. (Owner: Maya Chen)
- Instrument routing simulator with real traffic traces for 2 customers to validate model (Owner: Serving-runtime eng, ticket ENG-1299).
- Prototype Console preset for "Cost-Optimized" with spot-first=70%, quantize-fallback=true, cross-region=false (Owner: product-hosted-api).

Notes to reviewers
- This is informal and contains approximations; aim is to get policy knobs and a runnable sheet that product/solutions can use in Q2 proposals.
- Please comment on the spot availability assumption and any recent contract pricing that changes on-demand vs spot deltas.

Slack/backlinks
- Related Slack: #optimize-routing, thread link: https://slack-redwood.example/threads/C02R1234/optimize-routing
- Related Jira: PRO-4543 (console presets), ENG-1287 (routing-config schema)

Appendix: quick sensitivity mini-table (monthly cost vs spot availability)
Spot avail | Tiered-spot-first cost est | Delta vs baseline
70% | $8,200 | -59%
50% | $11,800 | -41%
30% | $16,900 | -15%

Small glossary
- Spot-first: routing preference to preemptible instances in other regions to save cost.
- Preempt window: time allowed to gracefully migrate before instances are reclaimed.
- KV cache hit rate: percent of requests for which we can avoid generation.

If helpful I can:
- convert the local CSV into a shareable google sheet with scenario toggles,
- run a quick analysis using last-quarter traffic from two representative customers and add realistic preemption curves.

-- Arjun
